challenges.name: strings-and-int-arithmetic-quiz
challenges.title: Predict the output: == on strings and int overflow
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way Java runs it: which strings are the same object, and when does int arithmetic overflow?

questions.explanation: strip() and toUpperCase() each return a NEW String built at runtime, so code is a different object from the "BOOK10" literal: == compares references and prints false, while equals compares the characters and prints true. Strings are immutable: strip() and toUpperCase() never change typed, so it still prints [ book10 ] with its spaces. "true true [BOOK10]" assumes == compares text and that the methods change typed in place; "true true [ book10 ]" gets immutability right but still treats == as a text comparison; "false true [BOOK10]" gets == right but assumes typed was changed.

int * int is computed in int, and 3,000,000,000 is above Integer.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647), so it wraps around to -1294967296 BEFORE any conversion to long happens. That is why long total = copies * price and long total = (long) (copies * price) both store -1294967296: the cast or the assignment widens a result that is already wrong. Casting ONE operand first, (long) copies * price or copies * (long) price, makes the multiplication itself a long multiplication, which gives 3000000000. Math.multiplyExact(copies, price) uses the int version (both arguments are int), so it does not wrap: it throws ArithmeticException: integer overflow. That is safer than a wrong number, but it stores nothing.

challenges.name: checkout-receipt-coupons
challenges.title: Write the Mekong Books checkout receipt
challenges.description: The checkout reads the coupon code the customer typed (spaces, any case, or nothing) and the order lines "QTY x UNIT_PRICE TITLE". Write four small methods: lineTotal (quantity x price as a long, safe for a 25,000-copy school order), discountPercent (BOOK10 is 10%, SCHOOL5 is 5%, compared as text, ignoring spaces around it and case), discountAmount (percent of the subtotal, rounded down to whole dong with integer arithmetic) and money ("3,000,000,000 VND" in any locale). The test runner reads the order from stdin and prints the receipt with your methods.
